steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
A transformer is a neural network architecture designed to model relationships within a sequence (words, tokens, etc.) without relying on recurrent loops.

1. Tokens in, vectors out  
   • Each input token is embedded as a numerical vector.  
   • Because the model has no notion of order by itself, a positional encoding is added to each vector so it can tell “word 1” from “word 5.”

2. Self-attention: “Who should I look at?”  
   • For every position the model builds three tiny vectors:  
     – Query (what I’m asking for)  
     – Key (how others describe themselves)  
     – Value (the content others can provide)  
   • A dot-product of Query with every Key produces scores saying how relevant every other token is to the current one.  
   • The scores are normalized (softmax) and used to mix the Value vectors into a single, context-aware representation for that position.  
   • Doing this several times in parallel with different learned projections gives multi-head attention, letting the model focus on multiple relationship types simultaneously.

3. Feed-forward refinement  
   • The attention output for each position is passed through a small feed-forward network, adding non-linearity and capacity.  
   • Residual connections and layer normalization keep training stable.

4. Stack and repeat  
   • Attention + feed-forward forms one layer; stacking many layers lets information flow across the entire sequence at varying depths.

5. Output  
   • The final contextual vectors feed into a classifier or a softmax over the vocabulary to predict the next token, translate text, answer questions, etc.

Because attention can look at all tokens at once, transformers train efficiently in parallel and capture long-range dependencies better than earlier recurrent models.
